column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/helm-monorepo-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHY THIS TABLE EXISTS
# On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran cargo-auto-release, reported
# SUCCESS, and published nothing: its `ship` job carried
# `&& !github.event.repository.private`, the repo was private, the job skipped,
# and a deliberate no-publish looked identical to a broken one. All sixteen
# substrate *-auto-release*.yml workflows touch `repository.private`, so every
# one of them gets a table saying which jobs must select for which input.
# WHAT THIS WORKFLOW ACTUALLY DOES WITH `repository.private` — the finding
# THIS workflow's single occurrence of `github.event.repository.private` is in
# `runs-on`, NOT in any `if:`. It is RUNNER ROUTING (private -> the
# self-hosted ARC pool (vars.PRIVATE_BUILDER_RUNNER) to avoid billed hosted minutes, public ->
# unmetered ubuntu-24.04), not a publish gate. So the graphql-synthesizer shape
# is structurally absent here: privacy changes WHERE the job runs, never WHETHER
# it runs. The two mandatory public/private rows below pin exactly that, and the
# private row is the one that would go red if somebody ever "harmonised" this
# workflow with the cargo one by copying that guard into the `if:`.
# That divergence is correct and deliberate, not an oversight: cargo-auto-release
# publishes to crates.io, where a private repo's code would leak publicly and a
# yank cannot be undone. This workflow publishes Helm charts to the org's OWN
# OCI registry (ghcr.io/pleme-io/charts), where a private chart's package stays
# private — per-package visibility is set out-of-band (see the workflow header).
# Refusing to publish from a private repo here would mean private chart repos
# such as helmworks-akeyless never ship at all.
# NO BUMP CASE — deliberately absent, because the workflow has no bump job to
# distinguish one with. A chart monorepo has no root Chart.yaml, so there is
# nothing to auto-bump; each chart's version is hand-bumped in its own
# Chart.yaml, and every push to main re-runs `nix run .#release` (forge helm
# release-all), which 404-probes each (name, version) and skips whatever is
# already on the registry. "Nothing was bumped" is therefore a RUNTIME no-op
# inside a job that still selects — not a job-selection state, and not
# something this linter can or should assert. If a bump job is ever added, this
# table gains a no-bump row in the same PR.
# UNMODELLED, stated so nobody reads a green run as more than it is: the
# `Fail the job if any upstream mirror failed` STEP is gated on
# `steps.mirror.outcome == 'failure'`, and step-level conditions are outside
# this linter's plane entirely (it asserts job selection). The mirror step's
# `continue-on-error: true` is likewise unmodelled. Both are load-bearing —
# see the workflow's own comments — and neither is covered here.
# Every context path a case's conditions touch must be declared, and an
# undeclared path is an error rather than an empty default. Only
# `github.actor` is actually read by the one `if:`; the
# `github.event.repository.private` value is declared on every row anyway so
# the public/private axis this sweep is about is visible in the table rather
# than only in this comment.
# 1. MANDATORY (public + would-publish): a human merge to main on a PUBLIC caller
# repo. `publish` must select — this is the ship-on-merge path itself.
public-repo-human-merge
# 2. MANDATORY (private + would-publish): the graphql-synthesizer row. On a
# PRIVATE caller repo `publish` must STILL select. Privacy routes this job to
# the ARC pool; it does not gate it. Expecting a skip here would be importing
# the crates.io posture into an OCI-registry workflow and would silently stop
# every private chart repo from shipping.
private-repo-human-merge
# 3. The only real guard on this workflow: the self-trigger break. `publish` is
# skipped when the pusher is github-actions[bot], so a bot commit (a consumer
# that later adds a bump step) cannot loop the release on itself.
bot-actor-self-trigger-guard
# ── DESTINATION VISIBILITY, MEASURED 2026-08-17 ────────────────────────────
# The no-guard posture above rests on the destination registry being private,
# which was previously asserted rather than checked. Measured today with an
# anonymous GHCR token (no credentials):
#   ghcr.io/pleme-io/charts/<a-private-chart>   HTTP 404
#   ghcr.io/pleme-io/charts/pleme-lib                 HTTP 403
#   ghcr.io/pleme-io/charts/lareira-akeyless-saas     HTTP 403
#   ghcr.io/pleme-io/helm/pleme-lareira               HTTP 403
#   ghcr.io/pleme-io/helm/ensaio                      HTTP 403
# Not publicly readable. So a private repo publishing here discloses nothing,
# and a privacy guard would only stop private chart repos from shipping —
# helmworks-akeyless among them.
# THIS WORKFLOW WAS BRIEFLY GUARDED AND THE GUARD WAS REVERTED THE SAME DAY.
# The sweep that guarded npm/python/crates counted `repository.private`
# occurrences without distinguishing a publish gate from runner routing, and
# swept this in with them. npm, PyPI and crates.io are public registries where
# a publish leaks source; this is not. The revert is the correction.
# What would change the answer: a caller overriding `registry` to a public
# host, or the namespace's per-package visibility being flipped. Neither is
# visible to a job condition, so re-measure rather than trusting this block.
